items.title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election
items.feed_excerpt: OpenAI’s Chris Lehane wants AI to define the 2028 election, proposing a new social contract that could benefit Americans while also advancing the AI giant’s own business interests.

items.title: Sequoia hits rewind, undoing 20 years of expansion
items.feed_excerpt: Sequoia is consolidating into a smaller, Bay Area–centered firm, shutting down the programs and offices it built during a 20-year expansion while announcing roughly $10 billion in new funds.

items.title: The ex-Secret Service agent who flipped a hacker is now raising a second $250M cybersecurity fund
items.feed_excerpt: Stephen Ward, a former Secret Service agent and Home Depot CISO, is preparing a second fund of roughly $250 million for Brightmind Partners.

items.title: Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
items.feed_excerpt: With Personal Finance in Claude, users can connect their bank and card accounts through Plaid and ask questions about their finances.

items.title: Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite
items.feed_excerpt: Following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion, food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company.

items.title: Bluesky hit peak usage for the year on election night
items.feed_excerpt: Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider said posts and likes doubled during to the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday.

items.title: Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery
items.feed_excerpt: Zipline raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart.

items.title: TikTok quietly launches a stand-alone TikTok Shop app
items.feed_excerpt: The app will offer personalized product recommendations, shopping through livestreams and short-form videos, app-exclusive deals, in-app checkout, order tracking, and customer support.

items.title: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
items.feed_excerpt: The deal is expected to support the development of DBX Agent Cloud, a new storage platform aimed at developers building AI models and agents.

items.title: Instagram brings Edits to desktop to take on CapCut
items.feed_excerpt: The move puts Edits in more direct competition with ByteDance's CapCut, the video-editing app Meta sought to challenge when it launched Edits last year.

items.title: ElevenLabs now lets users publish AI-generated music directly on SoundCloud
items.feed_excerpt: ElevenLabs said more than 25 million tracks have been generated using its music models.

items.title: Aina’s smart ring has a screen, a joystick, and a mic so you can talk to AI agents
items.feed_excerpt: Aina's ring can also take calls and help you dictate notes on your Mac.

items.title: RadianX promises solar-powered devices that never need charging
items.feed_excerpt: Today’s portable devices are too hungry to run on traditional solar panels, but RadianX says its perovskite cells promise to make charging obsolete in some cases.

items.title: Box taps Nvidia’s Nemotron for new agent-first content retrieval system
items.feed_excerpt: The system can supposedly answer queries four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used.

items.title: A YC startup is putting $1M behind 5 unsolved materials science problems for AI
items.feed_excerpt: While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials.

items.title: Agility is the first pure humanoid robot company on the stock market. Are you buying?
items.feed_excerpt: Agility arrives on the Nasdaq today as the first publicly traded pure-play humanoid robotics company.

items.title: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
items.feed_excerpt: Airbnb says its upcoming AI agent will help travelers plan trips, compare options, manage bookings, and get assistance throughout their stay.

items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots
items.feed_excerpt: Serve Robotics announced alonsgside its third-quarter earnings that it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services to offer customers its connectivity and data tools.

items.title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
items.feed_excerpt: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar, ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life.

items.title: Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder
items.feed_excerpt: Meta warns that growing political opposition to data centers could threaten future AI investments, as communities push back against massive infrastructure projects.

items.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
items.feed_excerpt: OpenAI's newest cybersecurity model comes out as AI labs face scrutiny of their work to protect digital infrastructure.

items.title: The New York Times reportedly in talks to buy Letterboxd for $330 million
items.feed_excerpt: Letterboxd, an online platform for movie lovers, has grown dramatically in recent years.

items.title: Meta, Google, and TikTok sue California AG over teen social media law
items.feed_excerpt: If it goes into effect next year, this California law would restrict social media access for children under 16.

items.title: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo
items.feed_excerpt: Despite its small size, Underdog's new model can generate both speech and music.

items.title: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
items.feed_excerpt: Physicl is trying to solve the sim-to-real gap with a pipeline originally built to market goods online.

items.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027
items.feed_excerpt: Elon Musk said the company will use the factory space to make more Cybercabs.

items.title: At least 10 local governments have moved to drop Flock’s surveillance cameras since summer
items.feed_excerpt: The concerns range from privacy to how data is shared (and with whom) to procurement concerns.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
items.feed_excerpt: Clutch, backed by Lightspeed and SignalFire, was last valued at $85 million, according to a source.

items.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
items.feed_excerpt: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.

items.title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent
items.feed_excerpt: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.

items.feed_excerpt: Democrats’ historic victories in this week’s U.S. midterm elections could also transform the tech industry. The public voted on 41 data center-related ballot measures on Tuesday — in all but one, the majority voted to impose more restrictions on data center development. items.title: Pentagon offers battery startup 6K $250M loan to build US factory
items.feed_excerpt: The Pentagon has conditionally approved a $250 million loan to help 6K scale up its microwave-plasma battery material manufacturing process.

items.title: Fox completes its $22B acquisition of Roku
items.feed_excerpt: A few months after DOJ investigators were probing the deal, Fox just completed its $22B acquisition of the streaming giant Roku.

items.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
items.feed_excerpt: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.

items.title: After blocking Muse, Amazon now lets users text Alexa to help them shop
items.feed_excerpt: Amazon said that the feature will roll out to millions of users in coming weeks.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.feed_excerpt: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.

items.title: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple
items.feed_excerpt: There are now 100,000 Duo-optimized apps, says Apple, and thousands more arrive daily.

items.title: Sequoia shutting down its Scouts program marks the end of an era
items.feed_excerpt: Sequoia pioneered the scouts model and many VC firms followed suit, but a consensus now seems to be forming that the model has reached limits in its current form.

items.title: From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech
items.feed_excerpt: After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the markets are about to do.

items.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
items.feed_excerpt: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.

items.title: Binance CFO is leaving to ‘pursue a new venture’ after $6.3 billion hack
items.feed_excerpt: The announcement comes barely more than a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance users.

items.title: Amazon’s new basic Kindle proves you don’t need all the bells and whistles
items.feed_excerpt: Amazon's redesigned basic Kindle costs more than before, but its lighter build and improved display make a compelling case for skipping the pricier models.
